newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Life sees "successful" full-yr outcome.
newsitem.headline: Irish Life sees "successful" full-yr outcome.

text.p: Ireland's largest assurance group Irish Life Plc said on Thursday that trading performance had continued to be positive since June and it was on target to achieve its objectives for the full-year.
"Trading performance continues to be positive since June and we expect another successful outcome to the year as a whole," Chairman Conor McCarthy said in Irish Life's half-year results statement.
Irish Life's key profit measure, embedded value earnings, rose to 48 million punts in the first half of 1996 versus 34 million in the first half the previous year.
Total group sales for the period fell 11 percent to 204.5 million punts.
"This relates almost entirely to our business in the U.S. where sales fell...principally as a result of the contraction of the fixed annuity market due to low interest rates," McCarthy said.
U.S. sales fell to 61.3 million punts from 107 million in the same period last year.
"Regular premium life sales in the U.S. however continue to grow steadily and are up eight percent for the period," McCarthy said.
In Ireland, total sales were up seven percent at 107.8 million punts. A 14 percent rise in single premium sales was partly offset by a fall of 11 percent in recurring premium sales.

"We are, however, confident that our new range of defined contribution pension plans together with the recently launched range of regular premium savings and investment products...will increase our regular premium business," McCarthy said.
Irish Life Managing Director David Kingston said the comapny had made significant progress on its policy review exercise and had also made progress on reforming its field force.

"Changes in our distribution in Ireland have been somewhat slower than planned and have obviously impacted on sales," McCarthy said. "However, considerable progress has been made in securing the full agreement of our field force to these changes and we are confident that agreement will be finalised shortly."
